text.p: Bonds tightened the gap with Bunds at the long end as the periphery markets were given a strong boost by a lively performance by Italy.
But a feeling that the Bank of Portugal will not cut interest rates again in the short-term is limiting the room for immediate gains at the shorter end of the curve, they added.
"The 10 years closed very well supported thanks to the excellent performance of the (Italian) BTP and the stronger escudo," said one fixed-income trader.

"The long end closed buyer...we are still some way from the record low spread with the Bund (50 basis points) and the chances of the single currency have improved after the (Amsterdam) summit," said another trader.

For the moment, the shorter end would trade quietly, with prices capped by the absence of any prospect of a rate cut soon, traders said. "For the coming days, the curve is going to remain flat. Then it is going to steepen. You have to remember that Spain could cut rates next week," said the first trader.
The spread between the two and 10-year markets narrowed to 113 basis points on Wednesday from 115.
